battle.name: 巴西獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 伯南布哥、巴拉伊巴與巴伊亞海岸
battle.brief: 一八二一年里斯本召回王室，葡軍在巴西只剩零散守軍與港口據點；戰火自一八二二年六月在米納斯、伯南布哥與巴伊亞同時升級，同年九月七日佩德羅在伊皮蘭加宣布獨立，至一八二四年一月葡軍盡撤。卡面這件輪發手槍代表軍官那一層火力：它不列於前排，站在步槍隊之後，替指揮官補上最後的距離。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 一八二二年開打時，葡萄牙一方在巴西只剩駐軍體系的殘餘：來自里斯本的一支陸軍分遣隊，指揮官是若熱·德·阿維萊斯中將，兵力約兩千人，另有散布在港口城市的守備部隊與一支海軍分遣艦隊，據點包括累西腓、薩爾瓦多、聖路易斯、貝倫與蒙得維的亞。葡軍在巴西的指揮鏈條以里斯本為最高點，總督與參謀權集中，補給全靠海運，內陸長期無援可待。另一方是新生的巴西：佩德羅親王在米納斯吉拉斯、聖保羅與里約熱內盧一帶組建國民義勇隊與正規軍，聖保羅鄉土軍隊是其中編制最完整的一支；海軍方面，一八二二年底從里約熱內盧接管十一艘原葡軍大小艦艇，又在倫敦與利物浦秘密招募五十名軍官及五百名水手，蘇格蘭人托馬斯·科克倫出任海軍總司令。巴西領土上還夾著兩股勢力：其一是害怕自身主權被架空的省級貴族與軍人，其代表是一八二四年伯南布哥的「赤道邦聯」共和派；其二是原本打算收拾佩德羅的葡軍部分軍人。英國、美國與拉普拉塔聯合省在交戰中保持中立，卻以貸款、軍火與志願兵的形式偏向巴西一邊，戰後才陸續承認新國。葡軍在巴伊亞與伯南布哥的守備只是數個營編與砲兵連，缺員缺糧全靠海運接濟；巴西一方的軍隊則由葡軍留巴西的部分殖民部隊、新募的步兵營與各省義勇隊拼成，軍中亦確有法國、德國與義大利的流亡者擔任軍官與教官。佩德羅親王自任軍隊最高統帥，另設專責收復巴伊亞的遠征軍；海路與驛信把里約同各省連成一條指揮線，命令與補給的快慢，最後決定了各條戰線誰先站穩。
countriesEn: By the time the fighting began in 1822, the Portuguese side in Brazil was reduced to the residue of the colonial military system: a Portuguese army detachment from Lisbon under General Jorge de Avilez, roughly two thousand men, together with garrison troops scattered among the port cities and a Portuguese naval squadron, holding positions at Recife, Salvador, São Luís, Belém and Montevideo. The Portuguese command chain in Brazil still ran upward to Lisbon, with authority concentrated in the governor and his staff, supply carried entirely by sea, and almost no reinforcement reaching the interior. The other side was the newborn Brazil: around the prince regent Pedro, in Minas Gerais, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, loyal militias and a regular army were raised, the São Paulo provincial force being the most complete in organisation; for the navy, eleven former Portuguese warships of every size fell into Brazilian hands at Rio de Janeiro in late 1822, and fifty officers and five hundred seamen were recruited in secret in London and Liverpool, with the Scotsman Thomas Cochrane appointed commander in chief of the navy. Two further forces sat between the two sides: provincial elites and soldiers who feared that their own sovereignty was being hollowed out, represented by the republican Confederation of the Equator in Pernambuco in 1824; and those Portuguese soldiers who had intended to finish off Pedro instead. Britain, the United States and the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata remained formally neutral, yet leaned toward Brazil through loans, arms and volunteers, and recognised the new state one after another only after the war. The Portuguese garrisons at Bahia and Pernambuco amounted to a few battalions and companies of artillery, their losses in men and food made good only by sea; the Brazilian army, for its part, was pieced together from part of the Portuguese colonial troops left in Brazil, newly raised infantry battalions and provincial militias, and it certainly contained French, German and Italian exiles serving as officers and instructors. The prince regent was commander in chief of the armies in person, with a separate expeditionary force raised to retake Bahia; the sea lane and the courier service tied Rio to the provinces into a single chain of command, and the speed of orders and supply decided on each front which side found its footing first.
people: 佩德羅·德·阿爾坎塔拉·布蘭卡，即後來的佩德羅一世，戰前是巴西攝政親王，宮廷與政界都視他為王位繼承人；正是他在一八二二年一月九日宣告留下不走，九月七日行軍途中在伊皮蘭加的小溪旁聽到里斯本召回他的消息，當場扯下象徵葡萄牙的藍白臂章，拔劍宣誓，巴西人稱之為「伊皮蘭加的呼喊」。他的妻子奧地利出身的瑪麗亞·萊奧波蒂娜站在巴西一邊，敦促他留在美洲；他的顧問若澤·博尼法西奧·德·安德拉達於一八二二年一月十八日出任王國與外交大臣，被視為起草獨立外交文件的人，後人稱其為「國父」。自由派領袖若阿金·貢薩爾維斯·萊多主張召開制憲議會，與博尼法西奧一路互有張力。葡軍方面的核心人物是若熱·德·阿維萊斯：一八二二年一月他率約兩千名士兵在里約熱內盧的城堡山抗拒佩德羅的解散令，隨後退往尼泰羅伊等待船隻回國。巴西方面最重要的非王室人物是蘇格蘭海軍軍官托馬斯·科克倫，他率六艦分隊封鎖薩爾瓦多，以佯攻與假情報迫使葡軍放棄巴伊亞、馬拉尼昂與帕拉，又派帕斯科·格倫費爾與約翰·泰勒追擊撤退船隊。地方武力方面，伯南布哥鄉土首領法雷·卡內卡與米格爾·德·弗里亞斯於一八二四年率領共和派起事，最終被政府軍在雅布蒂卡巴一帶平定。在巴伊亞主持巴西軍攻勢的是法國出身的將領拉巴蒂；科克倫此前先後為智利與俄羅斯效力，帶來歐洲海軍的封鎖與操練手法，他招募的五十名軍官多是拿破崙戰爭後失去職位的歐洲人。據當時記述，佩德羅對願意放下武器的葡軍士兵許諾赦免並資助回國，據說有數百人接受條件離隊，戰爭的勝負因此有很大一部分決定在港口守軍的士氣與去留。包圍城堡山的是王家警察衛隊與被臨時徵召的民兵；佩德羅在宣布獨立後兩個月內走遍里約熱內盧、聖保羅與米納斯，召集各地代表與民兵首領，把個人聲望變成省級的擁戴；九月七日至十月十二日加冕之間，站上仍在爭論他該不該稱王。
peopleEn: Pedro de Alcântara Braganza, later Pedro I, was prince regent of Brazil before the war, and both court and political class looked on him as the heir to the throne; it was he who declared on 9 January 1822 that he would stay, and on 7 September, receiving on the road the news from Lisbon that he was being summoned home, he tore off the blue-and-white armband that symbolised Portugal, drew his sword and swore the oath that Brazilians call the Cry of Ipiranga. His wife, Maria Leopoldina of Austria, stood on the Brazilian side and urged him to remain in the Americas. His adviser José Bonifácio de Andrada, appointed minister of the kingdom and of foreign affairs on 18 January 1822, is remembered as the man who drafted the diplomatic acts of independence and was later called the Father of the Fatherland. The liberal leader Joaquim Gonçalves Ledo argued for a constituent assembly, and he and Bonifácio were in constant tension. The central figure on the Portuguese side was Jorge de Avilez: in January 1822 he led some two thousand soldiers who, on the hill of the Castle in Rio de Janeiro, refused the prince's order to disband, and were then pushed back to Niterói to await shipping home. The most important non-royal figure on the Brazilian side was the Scottish naval officer Thomas Cochrane, who with six ships blockaded Salvador, used feints and false intelligence to force the Portuguese out of Bahia, Maranhão and Pará, and sent Pascoe Grenfell and John Taylor to chase the withdrawing convoys. Among the local forces, the Pernambuco chiefs Frei Caneca and Miguel de Frias led the republican rising of 1824, which the government army finally broke at Jabuticaba. The Brazilian offensive in Bahia was led by the French-born general Labatut; Cochrane had served Chile and Russia before, bringing European practice in blockade and drill, and many of the fifty officers he recruited were Europeans left without employment after the Napoleonic wars. Contemporary accounts have it that Pedro offered pardon and passage home to Portuguese soldiers who would lay down their arms, and that several hundred took the terms and left the colours; the outcome of the war therefore depended in good part on the morale of the men who garrisoned the ports and on whether they chose to stay or to go. Those who surrounded the hill of the Castle were the royal police guard and militia called out at short notice; in the two months after the declaration Pedro travelled through Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo and Minas Gerais, calling in the provincial deputies and the chiefs of the militias, turning personal prestige into provincial allegiance; and between 7 September and the acclamation of 12 October the question of whether he ought to be king at all was still being argued.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是輪發手槍，十六世紀初的西班牙製品：最早的後膛手槍，靠發條與棘輪把擊錘鎖在待擊位置，鑰匙扳機一轉即完成上膛，機構複雜、造價昂貴，因此只配給火槍隊的軍官與親近衛兵，從不列為制式陣列兵器。巴西獨立戰爭爆發於一八二二至一八二四年，該機構早已被燧發手槍取代，與之對應的階層是雙方軍官、鼓手與佩德羅親王儀仗護衛所攜的燧發手槍；卡面選用輪發手槍，正是要標示這一位置——它不是打全線的火力，而是指揮官的最後一發與貼身防衛。史料並無留下輪發手槍參與本役的實戰記錄，此卡以同類兵器的軍官階層作代表，不作實物指涉。真正決定陣線厚度的仍是後排的步槍：巴西義勇隊多配滑膛燧發步槍，騎兵用燧發卡賓槍與馬刀，砲兵以四磅、六磅與十二磅野戰砲為骨架，各營編配不一，攻城與守城則靠騎砲與臼砲。海上方面，科克倫接手大小十一艘葡軍舊艦，用巡防艦、雙桅縱帆船與小型帆船分擔封鎖、追擊與偵察，另有英格蘭運來的木料在里約熱內盧船塢趕造新艦。海路是這場戰爭的命脈：兵員、糧食、砲彈與船員全靠它，內陸義勇隊只靠騾馬與畜力車運糧，糧源線一旦被切斷，圍城就會自行解體。再往後一步，十六世紀末的毒蛇式自擊發機構（要打開槍機先要按住槍機的按桿）取代了鑰匙，十七世紀的燧發機（以燧石打火）又令手槍可以做得更小更可靠，輪發手槍自此退為軍官與衛兵的收藏與儀仗之物；到一八二〇年代的巴西，這一階層早已改用燧發手槍。步兵火力方面，巴西義勇隊的步槍規格極不統一，多數是滑膛燧發步槍配套筒刺刀，部分民兵只有獵槍、砍刀甚至農具；砲兵除野戰砲外另有臼砲與攻城用的重砲，守城一方則靠城牆射孔與臨時修築的胸牆。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the wheellock pistol, a Spanish piece from the early sixteenth century: the earliest breech-loading handgun, in which a spring and ratchet lock the hammer back and a key on the trigger winds the mechanism, so complicated and so costly that it was issued only to the officers of the musketeer companies and their close guards and never became a standard weapon in the line. The Brazilian war of independence broke out between 1822 and 1824, by which time that mechanism had long been superseded by the flintlock, and the corresponding rank on both sides was the flintlock pistol carried by officers, drummers and the ceremonial guard of the prince regent; the wheellock on the card is chosen precisely to mark that place in the order of battle — it is not the firepower of the line but the officer's last shot and his personal defence. No record survives of a wheellock pistol actually taking part in this war, so the card represents the officer echelon through the same class of weapon rather than a physical piece. What really decided the thickness of a line was still the musket in the rear rank: the Brazilian militias were mostly armed with smoothbore flintlock muskets, the cavalry with flintlock carbines and sabres, and the artillery with field guns of four, six and twelve pounds in varying establishment, heavier pieces being used for siege and defence. At sea Cochrane inherited eleven old Portuguese hulls of every size, dividing blockade, pursuit and reconnaissance among frigates, brigs and small sailing craft, while new ships were built at the Rio de Janeiro yards from timber shipped from England. The sea lane was the lifeline of this war: troops, food, powder and crews all moved by it, and the inland militias shifted grain on mules and animal-drawn carts only; once the supply route was cut, a siege came apart by itself. One step further, the serpentine mechanism of the late sixteenth century, in which the lock had to be held back by a lever, replaced the key, and the seventeenth-century flintlock, firing from a piece of flint, made the pistol smaller and more reliable, so the wheellock retreated to the collection and the ceremonial of officers and guards; by the 1820s in Brazil that rank had long been using flintlock pistols. On the infantry side the Brazilian muskets were of no standard at all, most of them smoothbore flintlocks with socket bayonets, while some militiamen carried only fowling pieces, machetes and even farm tools; besides the field guns the artillery had mortars and heavy pieces for siege, and the defenders relied on loopholes in the walls and on breastworks thrown up in haste.
tactics: 巴西獨立戰爭少有正面會戰，多數場面是「以不打求打」的消耗。義勇隊與游擊隊的常用手段是切斷葡軍的沿海補給：奪佔鄉間渡口，伏擊運糧船隊，在丘陵與林緣等落單的縱隊，交手後立即退回內陸，不與葡軍守備隊糾纏。葡軍守城時倚賴據點的城牆與砲位，把主力壓縮在城內，靜待里約熱內盧派船解圍，因此巴西方面的攻城多半不是強攻，而是「封海加封路」的雙重絞殺：一邊以巡防艦封鎖港口切斷糧源，一邊由義勇隊在陸上消耗騾馬與援軍的通行。海軍總司令科克倫用得最順手的是奇襲與心理戰，他曾放出龐大艦隊即將抵達的情報，誘使聖路易斯與貝倫守軍棄城，又用假艦隊逼退瓜納巴拉海灣的分遣隊。伊皮蘭加一役與佩德羅在聖保羅、里約熱內盧之間的行軍，則是唯一一場以儀仗式武裝完成的行動：親王的儀仗衛隊沿途集合，隨行者多為軍官與護衛，佩德羅在受訊當場宣布獨立，整個過程更像一次檢閱而非會戰。正面較量的樣本是巴伊亞：佩德羅親王率領的巴西軍隊與葡軍守備隊在累西腓至伊塔帕里卡一線反覆拉鋸，雙方都靠白天的炮擊與夜間的襲擊，換取下一個清晨的立足點。一八二三年五月四日，巴伊亞灣內再戰，葡軍在退卻中被切斷，最後一批守軍在幾日內登船北撤；巴西軍隊在巴伊亞灣內用小艇與浮橋分割敵陣的做法，說明這一階段的戰爭靠的是水陸配合而非正面衝鋒。
tacticsEn: The Brazilian war of independence saw few set-piece battles; most of the action was a war of attrition fought without a real engagement. The standard methods of the militias and guerrilla bands were to cut the Portuguese coastal supply: seizing country crossings, ambushing supply convoys, waiting in the hills and along the edge of the forest for isolated columns, and then falling back inland at once instead of getting entangled with Portuguese garrison troops. When besieged, the Portuguese relied on the walls and gun positions of their strongpoints, compressed their strength inside the walls and waited for a squadron from Rio de Janeiro, so that the Brazilian sieges were rarely assaults but a double strangulation of sea and land: a squadron of frigates sealing the port to cut off food, while the militias on land wore down the mules and the road used by relief columns. Cochrane was at his best in surprise and psychological warfare: he let it be known that an enormous fleet was on its way and tempted the garrisons of São Luís and Belém into evacuating, and he drove off the detachment in Guanabara Bay with phantom squadrons. The episode at Ipiranga and Pedro's march between São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro was the one action carried out with ceremonial arms: the prince's guard of honour assembled along the road, his companions were mostly officers and protectors, and the declaration of independence was made on the spot, the whole thing closer to a parade than a battle. The sample of open fighting is Bahia, where the army led by the prince regent Pedro and the Portuguese garrison fought back and forth along the line from Recife to Itaparica, each side trading gunfire by day and raids by night for a foothold the next morning. On 4 May 1823 there was fighting again inside the Bay of All Saints, the Portuguese were cut off during their retreat and the last garrison shipped out northward within a few days; the Brazilian practice of dividing the enemy position with boats and pontoons inside the bay shows that this stage of the war was fought by combined sea and land movement rather than by frontal assault. The Bahia front shows the methods of both sides best: on the night of 8 November 1822 the Portuguese sortied and attacked, the Brazilian militia was briefly scattered by the torches, the Portuguese lost their direction in the darkness and were back inside the walls before dawn, the sources putting their losses at several hundred dead and a little over a dozen prisoners, and the Brazilian army afterwards took the initiative back through combined sea and land pressure and continuous bombardment. The war was therefore decided not by any single engagement but by who could hold the ports and who could cut the other's supply line, which is why Cochrane made the navy rather than the army his main instrument.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，先列可靠的幾組：一八二二年一月，葡萄牙在巴西的陸軍分遣隊約兩千人，退守城堡山時被約一萬名武裝的巴西民兵與王家警察圍住，最後由里約熱內盧方面支付船票送走；一八二二年底被巴西接管的葡萄牙艦艇共十一艘，構成新海軍的骨幹。科克倫在倫敦與利物浦秘密招募五十名軍官與五百名水手，多為拿破崙戰爭老兵；一八二三年四月一日他率六艘船自里約熱內盧出發前往巴伊亞，接戰失利後改為封鎖，葡軍最終於七月二日乘約九十艘船的船隊棄城；到十一月巴西北部盡入巴西控制，十二月蒙得維的亞撤軍，至一八二四年一月境內再無葡軍。戰役規模方面，官方檔案與當時報導多已散佚，現代學者按各地戰鬥記錄推估，雙方作戰陣亡合計約五千七百至六千二百人；戰事前後約二十二個月，作戰地帶橫跨伯南布哥、巴拉伊巴、巴伊亞、馬拉尼昂、帕拉、西斯普拉塔，以及更南的聖保羅與里約熱內盧。人口與經濟面，巴西自由人口在獨立之初文盲率約九成，奴隸制度是最大的產業支柱，既是蔗糖與咖啡出口的地基，也是拿破崙時代英國輸出的最終市場。凡未能核實者本段不列。距離與時間方面，巴西南北縱長數千公里，陸軍自里約熱內盧南下至巴伊亞的路程超過一千五百公里，靠騾馬與牛車行軍；海上由里約到薩爾瓦多與北方各港口，靠雙桅船與巡防艦接續，數月的封鎖才能累積成效果。人口方面，一八二〇年代巴西總人口約三百萬上下（各家說法不一），其中被奴役的非洲人口佔比甚高，每年仍有好幾萬人被運抵巴西的港口。「赤道邦聯」的起事則在幾個月內即被平定。官方敘述常把這場衝突算成四年（自一八二二年宣布獨立到一八二五年簽約），但真正交火集中在二十二個月之內；自佩德羅在伊皮蘭加宣布獨立到最後一批葡軍登船離開，約十六個月。海軍自里約到薩爾瓦多的航程約一千四百公里，北方行動更遠，靠河口的小艇深入亞馬遜水道。
dataEn: Not many figures can be checked, so here are the reliable ones. In January 1822 the Portuguese army detachment in Brazil numbered about two thousand men; when it withdrew to the hill of the Castle it was surrounded by some ten thousand armed Brazilians led by the royal police guard, and was finally sent away at the expense of the Rio de Janeiro authorities. In late 1822 eleven Portuguese ships were taken over by Brazil, forming the backbone of the new navy. Cochrane recruited fifty officers and five hundred seamen in secret in London and Liverpool, many of them veterans of the Napoleonic wars; on 1 April 1823 he sailed from Rio de Janeiro with six ships for Bahia, and after an unsuccessful engagement fell back on blockade, the Portuguese finally abandoning the city on 2 July in a convoy of about ninety ships. By November the whole of northern Brazil was under Brazilian control, in December the Portuguese evacuated Montevideo, and by January 1824 there were no Portuguese troops left on Brazilian soil. On the scale of the war, official files and the reports of the day have largely been lost, and modern scholars, working from surviving registers of individual engagements, put total killed in action on both sides at roughly 5,700 to 6,200. The war itself lasted about twenty-two months, and the fighting covered Pernambuco, Piauí, Bahia, Maranhão, Pará and Cisplatina, with São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro further south. On the demographic and economic side, the free population of Brazil was around ninety per cent illiterate at independence, and slavery was the largest industry of the country, the foundation of the sugar and coffee exports and the final market of British output in the Napoleonic era. Nothing that could not be verified is listed here. On distance and time, Brazil is several thousand kilometres long from north to south, and the march of the army from Rio de Janeiro down to Bahia runs to more than fifteen hundred kilometres, carried on mules and ox carts; at sea the passage from Rio to Salvador and to the northern ports was kept up by brigs and frigates in relay, and only months of blockade added up to an effect. On population, the total population of Brazil in the 1820s was of the order of three million, the various estimates differing, and a very large share of it was enslaved African population, with tens of thousands still landing at Brazilian ports each year. The Confederation of the Equator rising, by contrast, was settled within a few months. Official accounts often reckon the conflict as four years, from the declaration of independence in 1822 to the signature in 1825, but the fighting itself was concentrated into twenty-two months; from the Cry of Ipiranga to the departure of the last Portuguese troops by sea was about sixteen months. The passage from Rio to Salvador is some fourteen hundred kilometres, the northern operations further still, carried into the Amazon channels by boats worked from the river mouth.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層加錯在一起。第一層是宗主國的轉向：一八二〇年葡國自由革命爆發，里斯本召開制憲議會，國王若昂六世被迫於一八二一年四月二十六日帶王室返回歐洲，留下的巴西由攝政親王佩德羅代管；同年九月三十日議會通過法令，把巴西各省政府直接隸屬里斯本，並下令親王回歐、只保留一個省級總督的職位。對習慣了自一八〇八年以來「朝廷在里約熱內盧」的巴西人而言，這等於把一八一五年才拿到的王國地位重新貶回殖民地。第二層是葡軍在巴西的存在本身：奉命執行解散令的指揮官阿維萊斯拒絕聽命，兩千人一度盤踞里約熱內盧城中的城堡山，葡軍的存在讓每一個巴西省都相信隨時可能被重奪。第三層是巴西自身的政治成熟：一八〇八年設法院、一八一五年封王國、一八二〇年以來自由派與邦法西奧派在報紙與沙龍裡公開討論憲法，佩德羅身邊已聚起一批能立法、能理財的行政人才。一旦里斯本宣布要收回王冠，本國菁英便認定再也沒有折衷的空間，於是主權的問題由談判轉為兵戎。經濟上同樣有怨：里約朝廷在聖保羅的評議會制度本已令巴西菁英看到自身的治理能力，而里斯本仍只准巴西的產品經葡國港口輸出，開放通商口岸的成果隨國王回國而逐步收緊，自由派與邦法西奧派所爭的其實是主權背後的關稅與航運權。
causeEn: The war came out of three layers of grievance tangled together. The first was the turn taken by the mother country: the liberal revolution in Portugal in 1820 produced a constituent assembly in Lisbon, and King João VI was forced to leave with the royal family for Europe on 26 April 1821, leaving Brazil in the hands of the prince regent Pedro. On 30 September the same year the assembly passed a decree subordinating the governments of the Brazilian provinces directly to Lisbon, ordered the prince back to Europe and reduced him to a mere provincial governor. For Brazilians accustomed since 1808 to a court sitting in Rio de Janeiro, this was a demotion of the kingdom status won in 1815 straight back to colony. The second layer was the presence of the Portuguese army in Brazil itself: the commander sent to enforce the disbanding order, Avilez, refused to obey, and two thousand men occupied the hill of the Castle in Rio de Janeiro, so that every Brazilian province lived with the certainty that it might be reconquered at any time. The third layer was Brazil's own political maturity: a court of appeals established in 1808, a kingdom proclaimed in 1815, and from 1820 an open public debate on constitutions in the press and the salons, with a circle of administrators around Pedro who knew how to legislate and how to finance a state. Once Lisbon announced that the crown would be taken back, the local elite concluded that no compromise remained, and the question of sovereignty passed from negotiation to arms. The grievance was economic as well: the deliberative assembly at São Paulo under the Rio court had already shown the Brazilian elite what it could govern, yet Lisbon still insisted that Brazilian produce leave through Portuguese ports, and the opening of the ports was gradually reversed as the king went home; what the liberals and the Bonifacians were really arguing over was the tariff and the shipping rights behind the word sovereignty.
impact: 戰爭結束後，巴西沒有一夜之間變成另一個國家：君主制、奴隸制、大莊園與單一作物經濟原封不動地留了下來，獨立更像一次政權轉移而非社會重構。直接後果是巴西擁有了自己的陸軍與海軍，一八二二年在里約熱內盧成立的艦隊從無到有地養出一支能遠航的分隊，此後數十年在南北美洲的航道與爭端中都是一支正式力量；外交上則換來承認的次序：拉普拉塔聯合省最早，隨後是美國與西非的貝寧王國，葡萄牙於一八二五年八月二十九日在里約熱內盧條約中正式承認，條件是巴西支付一筆可觀的補償，並在與英國的商約中接受開放口岸與優惠關稅的安排，同時把禁止大西洋奴隸貿易寫成自己的義務。英國的資本與商品從此獲得進入巴西市場的制度保證，咖啡種植在里約熱內盧盆地與後來的聖保羅高地迅速擴張，巴西的世界市場地位由此奠定。另一面的代價是：一八二四年「赤道邦聯」共和派在伯南布哥的起義被政府軍以軍事手段迅速平定，說明這個帝國從一開始就選擇秩序而不是共和；一八二二年一度恢復奴隸買賣、限制外國商船的關稅法令，更顯示新生國家的保守性；對已進入巴西港口的非洲奴隸而言，獨立的代價是自由的希望在帝國體制內被一紙又一紙地拖延。制度上，新帝國把獨立前的省級隊伍整編成編制完整的線列步兵與砲兵，並在一八二四年頒布第一部憲法，把行政、立法與司法分開，聯邦制的省權條款最終只保留在形式上。外交上，巴西同英國的特殊關係由此定調：英國資本、英國商船與英國移民在往後半個世紀大量進入巴西，咖啡、橡膠與蔗糖的出口額都同英國市場綁在一起。
impactEn: When the war ended, Brazil had not become a different country overnight: monarchy, slavery, the great latifundia estates and the single-crop economy all stayed exactly as they were, and independence turned out to be a transfer of political power rather than a social reconstruction. The direct consequence was that Brazil now had an army and a navy of its own. The fleet organised at Rio de Janeiro in 1822 grew, from nothing, into a force able to make long voyages, and for decades afterwards counted as a regular power in the shipping lanes and disputes of South America. In diplomatic terms the sequence of recognition followed: the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata first, then the United States and the kingdom of Benin in West Africa, and finally Portugal itself in the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro of 29 August 1825, in exchange for a substantial compensation from Brazil and for commercial treaties with Britain opening Brazilian ports to British goods on preferential terms while making the ban on the Atlantic slave trade a Brazilian obligation. From then on British capital and British goods had the institutional guarantee of the Brazilian market, coffee planting expanded quickly in the Rio de Janeiro basin and later in the highlands of São Paulo, and the country's place in the world market was thereby settled. The other side of the ledger is the cost: the republican rising of the Confederation of the Equator in Pernambuco in 1824 was settled by government troops with military speed, showing that the empire had chosen order over a republic from the very start; the tariff decrees of 1822 that briefly reopened the slave trade and closed Brazilian ports to foreign shipping displayed the conservatism of the new state; and for the enslaved Africans already arriving in Brazilian ports, the price of independence was that the hope of freedom would be deferred document by document inside the empire. Institutionally, the new empire turned the provincial levies of the independence years into a regular line infantry and artillery, and issued its first constitution in 1824, separating the executive, the legislature and the judiciary, with the federal clauses for the provinces surviving in form rather than in substance. In foreign policy the special relationship with Britain was fixed: British capital, British shipping and British immigrants poured into Brazil over the following half century, and the export earnings of coffee, rubber and sugar were bound to the British market.
result: 打到一八二四年一月，境內再無成建制的葡軍，巴西事實上獨立；葡方守軍不是被攻滅，而是在封鎖與斷糧之下陸續登船北返，最後一批連同艦隊離開巴西。佩德羅在戰前已於一八二二年九月七日宣布獨立，同年十月十二日在桑塔娜廣場被加冕為巴西第一位皇帝，十二月一日加冕典禮完成，巴西帝國成立。外交收尾拖到一八二五年：八月二十九日葡巴代表在里約熱內盧簽署條約，正式承認巴西主權，葡方獲得一筆補償與若干貿易上的讓步，雙方往來並未斷絕。美洲其他殖民地由此多了一個可以照抄的樣本：一位留歐的宗主國王子在本地宣布獨立，以正規軍加義勇隊頂住母國軍隊，再用海軍封鎖切斷母國據點的補給，最後以談判收場。整套做法後來被委內瑞拉、大玻利維亞與阿根廷等地的運動者反覆引用，巴西的獨立也成為南美洲第一批共和與帝制並存的標本之一：它證明王室的轉向加上海軍的補給線，比任何一場正面會戰都更能決定一場殖民戰爭的勝負。法律上，巴西被視為聯合王國的延續而不是新邦，舊有的條約、債務與特許因此可以平移過去；葡屬西斯普拉塔與烏拉圭的爭端則被推遲，一八二五年起巴西與拉普拉塔聯合省另開戰端，與本役無關。
resultEn: By January 1824 there was no longer a formed Portuguese force on Brazilian soil and Brazil was independent in fact. The Portuguese garrisons were not destroyed in assault: they left ship by ship, northbound, one after another under blockade and hunger, and the last of them departed with the squadron. Pedro had already declared independence on 7 September 1822; on 12 October of the same year he was acclaimed on the Campo de Santana as the first emperor of Brazil, and on 1 December the coronation was completed, and the Empire of Brazil came into being. The diplomatic settlement dragged on until 1825: on 29 August the Portuguese and Brazilian representatives signed the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro, formally acknowledging Brazilian sovereignty, with a compensation and certain commercial concessions for Portugal, and relations between the two countries were not severed. The rest of the Americas now had a model to copy: a prince regent of the mother country, left behind in the colony, declaring independence in his own land, holding off the troops of the metropole with a regular army and loyal militias, and then cutting the supply of the mother country's strongpoints with a blockade at sea before ending the war by negotiation. The whole procedure was quoted and imitated again and again by the movements of Venezuela, Upper Peru and the Río de la Plata, and Brazilian independence became one of the first specimens in South America of a republic and an empire standing side by side. It demonstrated that a royal reversal of policy, added to a sea-borne supply line, decided the outcome of a colonial war far more effectively than any set-piece engagement. In law, Brazil was treated as the continuation of the United Kingdom rather than as a new state, so the old treaties, debts and concessions could simply be carried over; the dispute over Portuguese Cisplatina and Uruguay was postponed, and from 1825 Brazil and the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata fought a separate war of their own, unconnected with this one.
